statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 10 of 100 in the low band, fifteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now about thirty-six hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; fourteen of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress rises one point to 65, the base of the high band, as the weekend escalation record widened again this hour: the Houthis claimed a large barrage of ballistic missiles and drones against a Saudi base at Sharurah, UKMTO reported a further vessel struck inside the Strait of Hormuz, and reported Houthi control of Mocha and nearby Red Sea islands adds a Bab el-Mandeb dimension alongside the existing Hormuz blockade. Confidence holds at 86 on a full primary-source re-verification of levels, yields, oil, the event calendar and every published item cited here. Tail remains below the block threshold throughout the closed stretch and reaches the watch band only in the five slots around the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in fourteen of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the escalation that widened this hour is severe but is held in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path exists to be pathological. Third, the one genuine structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled restart, and the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than as a broad shutdown. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this reading.
headline: Thirty-six hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while the Houthis claim a large ballistic-missile and drone barrage on the Saudi base at Sharurah, UKMTO reports another vessel struck inside the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi forces are reported to hold Mocha and nearby Red Sea islands astride Bab el-Mandeb, Iraq has reopened two Iranian border crossings, and CME FedWatch still prices Wednesday's FOMC hike at 85.6 per cent.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour rather than carried over. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The last quote is timestamped 11 September at 17:15 New York time. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against this macro backdrop. Rates and oil are equally static: the Federal Reserve H.15 release still carries its 10 September observation at 4.00 per cent for the 3-month, 4.56 per cent for the 2-year, 4.95 per cent for the 10-year and 5.37 per cent for the 30-year, while WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent, and Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent.

The escalation record widened in both directions this hour. On the escalation side, Yemen's Houthis claimed a large barrage of ballistic missiles and drones against weapons depots and command facilities at a military base in Sharurah in Saudi Arabia's Najran region, with their spokesman warning of larger operations deeper inside the country; Saudi civil defence had reported a projectile strike at al-Tawwal that injured two people. UKMTO reported a further vessel struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with the crew evacuated after a fire, on top of the merchant vessel hit off Qeshm and Hengam that killed one person and wounded three. Reporting also places Houthi forces in control of the port of Mocha and nearby Red Sea islands, which puts a second maritime chokepoint at Bab el-Mandeb alongside the existing Hormuz blockade, while the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut after drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province. On the de-escalation side, Iraq reopened the al-Sheeb and Shalamcheh crossings with Iran on Sunday after Saturday's closures, Egypt's president urged Iran to de-escalate at their New Delhi meeting, and the Salalah meeting between Iran, Iraq and Gulf littoral states remains scheduled for Monday, though no signed Hormuz agreement is reported to be expected from it.

The macro checkpoint is unchanged and firm. CME FedWatch was last verified at 85.6 per cent for a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's FOMC, up from 48.4 per cent a month earlier, after August consumer prices rose 3.4 per cent year over year with core up 0.3 per cent month over month and producer prices came in above expectations. The meeting carries updated projections. Separately, Nasdaq's pro forma index data circulated late Friday points to SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 weight rising toward 2.82 per cent from roughly 1.28 per cent at a rebalance effective 21 September, an index-level flow checkpoint that sits beyond this horizon and is not treated as a priced outcome.

The reason this severity is held in Stress rather than Tail is the same as in the preceding hours. Tail measures a pathological price path that denies mean reversion; no such path exists to be measured, since there is no live tape, no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme to hold. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run, is stamped 06:48 UTC and therefore inside the 90-minute freshness bound, but reports a partial collection with its calendar section unavailable, so the calendar was rebuilt entirely from primary sources. Its usable sections are consistent with the verified picture and are used only as delayed supporting context: latest-session breadth positive across technology, communication services and consumer cyclicals, seven of eight megacaps higher, five of seven semiconductors higher, and delayed index futures marks last seen higher with the volatility future sharply lower and crude lower. None of that is live price-path evidence and none of it is used to justify the current Tail action, which rests on the absence of a tape. Every hourly news item published here was verified by direct fetch no later than this assessment timestamp; no scheduled future event is presented as news.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 08:00 UTC on 12 September to 07:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5, stepped to 6 in the second slot and held there for most of the window, reaching 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00 UTC and 9 in the final slot, in normal mode throughout and tracking the lengthening closure rather than any directional view; every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 57 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53, 56 and 57 to 64 by the close of the window as the weekend escalation reports accumulated and attention turned to the restart. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its 85 readings in the first half of the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window revises a past opinion with later information.
outlookSummary: Fourteen of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's fifteenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 10 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It is deliberately capped at 19 for the final three closed hours, because a market that cannot trade cannot produce the failed retracements the score measures. It then steps to 24 in the restart hour, the top of the watch band, and eases through 23, 22, 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, falling back through 19 and 18 to 17 by the close of the horizon. Those five watch-band slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday. Stress holds near 64 to 65 through the quiet Sunday stretch, then builds to a 70 peak at the restart on the unresolved two-chokepoint supply picture, the new attack vector against Saudi territory and thin reopening liquidity, before decaying to 64 across the Asian session. Confidence declines from 86 to a horizon low of 80 as distance from the last verified print grows, then recovers to 86 once a live tape exists again. Mode stays normal through the closure, is treated as event/whipsaw for the first two restart hours, mixed while early flow is assumed to normalise, and normal again by the end of the horizon. Monday's meeting in Salalah, Tuesday's Empire State index, Wednesday's retail sales and FOMC decision with projections, and the Nasdaq-100 rebalance effective 21 September all sit beyond the edge of this horizon and are treated as checkpoints rather than as priced outcomes.
